components.name: HV battery pack
components.parameters: Usable energy, voltage envelope, current limits and thermal state.
components.relationships: Inverter, BMS, charger and DC/DC converter.
components.limitation: Capacity and chemistry alone do not determine power capability or internal resistance.

components.name: Traction motor
components.function: Converts electrical power into mechanical torque.
components.parameters: Torque/speed envelope, rated power, voltage and efficiency map.
components.relationships: Inverter, reduction gearbox and driven wheels.
components.limitation: Topology does not specify efficiency; the retained model has no measured motor map.

components.name: Traction inverter
components.function: Controls motor phase currents from the DC bus.
components.parameters: DC voltage/current limits, switching losses and cooling.
components.limitation: SiC is a technology choice, not an automatic efficiency gain.

components.name: Battery management
components.function: Monitors battery state and enforces operating limits.
components.parameters: Cell voltages, temperatures, balancing and SOC estimation.
components.relationships: Battery cells, charger and torque control.
components.limitation: This foundation has no cell-level BMS, safety control or SOH estimator.

components.name: Reduction gearbox
components.function: Trades motor speed for wheel torque.
components.parameters: Reduction ratio, torque rating and mechanical efficiency.
components.limitation: An equivalent ratio does not describe axle topology or load transfer.

components.name: Thermal management
components.function: Moves heat to keep components within operating limits.
components.parameters: Coolant flow, heat transfer, temperature and auxiliary demand.
components.relationships: Battery, motor, inverter and cabin loads.
components.limitation: The existing model has no temperature state or validated thermal model.

components.name: DC/DC converter
components.function: Supplies the low-voltage electrical system from the HV bus.
components.parameters: Voltage range, load demand and conversion losses.
components.limitation: Low-voltage load and conversion dynamics are not simulated here.

components.name: Onboard charger
components.function: Converts AC supply to controlled DC battery charging.
components.parameters: AC input, DC voltage/current and cooling limits.
components.limitation: DC fast charging uses offboard conversion; it does not pass through the onboard AC converter.

components.name: Charging interface
components.function: Connects the vehicle to an external electrical supply.
components.relationships: Onboard charger for AC; battery DC path for fast charging.
components.limitation: Connector shape alone does not determine charging speed.

components.name: Auxiliary system
components.parameters: Accessory power, low-voltage battery and DC/DC supply.
components.relationships: Controls, lighting, pumps and HV enable functions.
components.limitation: Auxiliary demand must be modelled before attributing measured pack power to propulsion alone.

challenges.title: Driving range
challenges.problem: How far can stored energy take a vehicle?
challenges.physics: Usable battery energy must supply road work, drivetrain losses and auxiliary demand. Drag grows with speed squared; aerodynamic power grows with speed cubed.
challenges.technologies: Reduce drag area or mass, improve useful efficiency, or add usable capacity. Added capacity also adds mass and cost.
challenges.experiment: Compare drag area at identical prescribed speed and conditions.
challenges.classification: Established qualitative principles; proposed experiment, not an executed result

challenges.title: Battery degradation
challenges.problem: How does useful battery capability change with use?
challenges.physics: Capacity fade and resistance growth are different processes; temperature, SOC history and charge/discharge conditions matter.
challenges.technologies: Thermal control and managed operating windows address different stressors; a calibrated ageing model and longitudinal data are required.
challenges.experiment: Review the future SOH interface and evidence required before adding ageing.
challenges.classification: Established qualitative principles; proposed experiment, not an executed result

challenges.title: Charging time
challenges.problem: What limits energy transfer into the battery?
challenges.physics: The active limit is set by the pack acceptance curve, SOC/temperature, vehicle conversion limits and external supply.
challenges.technologies: AC onboard conversion and DC offboard charging have different bottlenecks. A constant advertised peak is not a charging curve.
challenges.experiment: Compare declared charging envelopes; time calculation is not available in foundation.
challenges.classification: Established qualitative principles; proposed experiment, not an executed result

challenges.title: Production cost
challenges.problem: Which design choices change component cost?
challenges.physics: Materials, manufacturing process, yields, scale and integration contribute; pack capacity alone cannot determine vehicle cost.
challenges.technologies: Use dated, region-specific component estimates with uncertainty; keep component subtotal, production cost and retail price separate.
challenges.experiment: Define a cost study and document the missing supplier/estimate evidence.
challenges.classification: Established qualitative principles; proposed experiment, not an executed result

challenges.title: Cold-weather performance
challenges.problem: Why can cold conditions affect usable performance?
challenges.physics: Temperature changes electrochemical kinetics and resistance; heating loads also consume pack energy.
challenges.technologies: Battery preconditioning, heat pumps and insulation involve energy and hardware trade-offs. No universal benefit is assumed.
challenges.experiment: Inspect which thermal inputs are missing from a voltage/current recording.
challenges.classification: Established qualitative principles; proposed experiment, not an executed result

challenges.title: Motor & inverter efficiency
challenges.problem: Where is energy lost between pack and wheels?
challenges.physics: Copper, magnetic, switching and conduction losses vary with load, speed, voltage and temperature.
challenges.technologies: Motor topology, semiconductor technology, gearing and control must be assessed with matched operating maps.
challenges.experiment: Prepare a controlled powertrain comparison; no label-based efficiency correction.
challenges.classification: Established qualitative principles; proposed experiment, not an executed result

challenges.title: Battery thermal management
challenges.problem: How is heat generation balanced against cooling?
challenges.physics: Electrical losses generate heat; heat capacity, thermal resistance and coolant conditions govern temperature evolution.
challenges.technologies: Liquid cooling, thermal interfaces and control add mass, power demand and complexity; data are required for a thermal network.
challenges.experiment: Inspect the thermal-model assumptions and unavailable temperature predictions.
challenges.classification: Established qualitative principles; proposed experiment, not an executed result

challenges.title: Materials & battery safety
challenges.problem: What constraints extend beyond energy capacity?
challenges.physics: Cell chemistry, material availability and thermal/electrical protection create distinct design constraints.
challenges.technologies: Material substitution, recycling and protection systems require supply-chain and safety evidence; research concepts are not production specifications.
challenges.experiment: Review chemistry choices without implying safety certification or quantified supply risk.
challenges.classification: Established qualitative principles; proposed experiment, not an executed result
